newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehbacher - min reserves could play new role in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Kuehbacher - min reserves could play new role in EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Friday that minimum reserve requirements could be useful to avert potential disturbances to monetary policy caused by cashless payments.

Speaking to a banking audience, Kuehbacher noted that it had not yet been decided if the future European Central Bank (ECB) would implement minimum reserves, which require banks to hold non-interest bearing deposits with the central bank.
The Bundesbank has been pushing for the ECB to use minimum reserves, as it does itself, despite complaints from German banks.

"Independent of their application under the framework we are familiar with, minimum reserves could well gain an important significance for monetary policy in a totally different form, if I look at the apparently endless move toward innovation in modern cashless payments."

Kuehbacher predicted an increased interest in cashless payments such as pre-paid cards, which are pre-loaded with small cash amounts, and "cyber money", used to acquire goods over the Internet, after the Euro was launched, since neither Euro cash nor coins would be immediately available.
Should such options result in any disturbance of monetary policy, a risk with Kuehbacher conceded was relatively minor, "minimum reserves would be a conceivable instrument to counteract this."
